market_laws.title: Resting size change decomposes into execution and cancellation
market_laws.statement: For a price level between two adjacent book snapshots: size_next = size_prev - traded_at_price - cancelled + added. Therefore net_passive_change = added - cancelled = size_next - size_prev + traded_at_price. A level that shrinks was either traded through or cancelled, and no sequence of book snapshots alone can tell which.
market_laws.condition: any price level observed in two adjacent order-book snapshots, with the aggressor-classified trade tape covering the interval between them
market_laws.mechanism_claim: Accounting identity of a limit order book price level. Every unit leaving a level is either executed against an aggressor or withdrawn by its owner; every unit arriving is a new passive order. It is true by construction and cannot decay.
market_laws.temporal_stability: permanent by construction; unaffected by regime, venue or sample
market_laws.review_criterion: Not reviewable as an empirical claim. It would only change if the definition of traded_at_price changed, for example if the tape stopped carrying aggressor side.

market_laws.title: A passive fill at the touch is followed by an adverse move exceeding the captured spread
market_laws.statement: A limit order resting at the touch and filled under a last-in-queue assumption is followed by a mid move against the filled side that is roughly threefold the half-spread it captured. Measured total is -1.07 bps before fees across both sides.
market_laws.condition: limit order placed at best bid or best ask at a book snapshot; filled only when cumulative aggressive volume at that exact price reaches the size displayed there at placement; 60s rest window before cancellation

market_laws.mechanism_claim: Adverse selection. A passive order is filled precisely when someone wants to trade against it, which is disproportionately when the filler holds the better short-term view. The liquidity provider is compensated by the spread and taxed by the information in the flow that lifts them.
market_laws.temporal_stability: unknown; measured on one symbol-day. The sign held on both sides and at both horizons, and t is large, but persistence across symbols and regimes is untested.
market_laws.review_criterion: Promote to replicated only after the same measurement across at least 20 symbols with chronological splits, a matched null and remove-best-symbol, all PASS. Mark broken if the sign reverses on any out-of-sample segment.

market_laws.title: Below roughly five minutes the round-trip cost exceeds one standard deviation of the move
market_laws.statement: Mid-move dispersion scales with horizon while the round-trip cost is a constant, so the share of moves able to pay the floor rises from 1.6 percent at 10 seconds to 48.1 percent at 5 minutes and 97.7 percent at one week. At 60 seconds the floor exceeds the 8.6 bps standard deviation of the move, which closes an unfiltered taker route at that horizon regardless of signal quality. At one week the relation has inverted completely: weekly single-symbol dispersion is 1397 bps, and the audited 16 bps floor is crossed by 97.7 percent of moves. The floor therefore binds through the holding horizon, not through the market.
market_laws.condition: mid-to-mid move measured on the recorded book for horizons up to 1h against the frozen 11 bps round-trip taker cost; the 1w row is measured on weekly closes for 87 symbols over 50 weeks against the audited 16 bps floor

null_test.reason: a dispersion measurement has no directional null; the relevant check is replication across symbols

market_laws.mechanism_claim: Variance of a price process grows with elapsed time while a fee and spread charge does not. The ratio of achievable move to fixed cost therefore improves monotonically with horizon, which sets a floor on the shortest tradeable horizon for a given cost structure.

market_laws.title: Perp-spot basis dispersion on liquid symbols is an order of magnitude below the two-leg cost floor
market_laws.statement: On liquid Bybit perpetuals the perp-spot basis is confined to a band far narrower than the 22 bps two-leg round trip. Basis standard deviation is 1.4-1.7 bps on XRP, BTC, SOL and ETH, so reaching the cost floor requires 13-15 standard deviations. Across the six most liquid symbols the basis exceeded 22 bps in 0.016 percent of 158,826 observations. Dispersion rises monotonically with illiquidity: only the two microcaps in the sample, TAC and VANRY, cross the floor with any regularity, at 41 and 57 percent. A separate and less certain observation is that the mean basis is negative on 17 of 18 symbols at roughly -5 to -8 bps; see notes, this may not be a market fact.

market_laws.horizon: 15m observation interval; mean-reversion half-life measured at 0.09-1.42h, median 0.20h

market_laws.mechanism_claim: Arbitrage between a perpetual and its spot leg is cheap and heavily contested on liquid symbols, so the basis is compressed to a band narrower than the cost of crossing it. The compression is itself the evidence of competition: dispersion scales inversely with liquidity, and only where the arbitrage is expensive or impossible does the basis widen past the floor.
market_laws.temporal_stability: Measured over 375 continuous days spanning several regimes. The ordering of symbols by dispersion was stable; no sub-period was examined separately.
market_laws.review_criterion: Promote to replicated only after (a) the alignment artifact in the notes is excluded, and (b) the dispersion result is reproduced on an independently constructed perp-spot join. Mark broken if any liquid symbol shows a sustained period with more than 1 percent of observations beyond 22 bps.

Two candidate explanations were considered. A timing lag between the spot and perp bar is the obvious one, but it is weakened by the evidence: a lag artifact scales with volatility, yet the mean sits in a narrow -5 to -8 band while the standard deviation varies twentyfold across symbols. A constant definitional offset -- perp mark price against spot last trade, or an index versus a venue price -- fits the observed near-constancy better. Neither was tested. The decision-relevant part of this law is the DISPERSION, which is robust to any additive offset: shifting every observation by 8 bps cannot move BTC from 13.7 sigma to within reach of the floor. The mean is recorded for completeness and must not be cited as evidence of backwardation until the review criterion is met. The t-statistic is reported with autocorrelation adjustment but cannot distinguish a real effect from a systematic offset, and so carries no weight on this question.

market_laws.title: Post-sweep continuation rises with sweep size and saturates below the cost floor
market_laws.statement: After a multi-level aggressive parent order, price continues in the sweep direction, and the size of that continuation rises monotonically with the sweep notional measured as a percentile rank within its own symbol. It also saturates: from 4.40 bps below the median to 8.27 bps for the largest one in a thousand, with the gain per doubling of percentile shrinking at the top. The relation is measured across nine bands with t running from 72.7 to 5.7. At no size does it reach the audited 16 bps round-trip floor. Conditioning it further on the pre-sweep depth response of the side about to be consumed adds nothing: a 5x5 double sort on within-symbol notional rank and depth-response rank is flat in the depth dimension at every size and at 60s, 300s and 900s, and the maximum of all 75 reportable cells is 10.27 bps.
market_laws.condition: multi-level parent sweeps reconstructed at a 100 ms burst gap on 10 Bybit symbols over 13 days; entry at the mid at sweep completion; notional ranked within symbol, never pooled across symbols
market_laws.horizon: 60s primary; the same ordering holds at 300s and 900s

Entering at completion collects only the remainder. Larger orders reveal more but also consume more of their own move before completion, which is why the relation rises and then flattens. The pre-sweep state of the consumed book side does not discriminate, which suggests the remaining move is dispersion rather than a conditional expectation.

market_laws.title: Weekly cross-sectional momentum in liquid crypto perps orders the quintiles but is bounded far below the published effect
market_laws.statement: Sorting liquid perpetuals into quintiles on trailing three-week return and holding one week produces a monotone ordering of forward returns -- 90, 101, 123, 169 and 181 bps across the five buckets over 100 non-overlapping rebalances. The long-short spread is 91.1 bps gross with a standard error of 61.7, so it cannot be distinguished from zero at t=1.48. It CAN however be distinguished from the published effect: Liu, Tsyvinski and Wu report 250 to 410 bps weekly, which sit 2.6, 3.4 and 5.2 standard errors above this estimate. An effect of the published magnitude is not present in this universe over this period. The payoff shape argues against the residual being real: the median is 21 bps against a mean of 91, only 51 percent of weeks are net positive, and at the 32 bps double-cost stress the net median is negative.
market_laws.condition: 43 Bybit perpetuals with a complete weekly close series from 2023-01-02 to 2026-07-27, 187 weeks; equal-weighted quintiles on trailing three-week return, one-week hold, no overlap; turnover measured at 43 percent long and 49 percent short per rebalance and charged at 16 bps per side

data_constraints.title: Historical funding archive carries settlement time, not publication time
data_constraints.statement: The historical funding archive contains a settlement timestamp but no publication or ingest timestamp; therefore using a value for a decision before settlement creates unprovable causality and a potential look-ahead.
data_constraints.scope_note: Applies to this dataset specifically. It is not a claim about historical funding archives in general, nor about any future forward-recorded funding series.
evidence: Schema carries exactly one time field per record: ts, alongside by_r, by_p, bi_r, bi_p, ok_r, ok_p. No publication field, no predicted-rate field, no ingest field.
All 691 BTCUSDT timestamps fall exactly on 00:00, 08:00 and 16:00 UTC, with zero off-schedule records. That is the Bybit funding settlement grid.

All ten per-symbol files were written between 2026-07-11T11:46:59Z and 11:47:06Z, one backfill batch, covering values from 2025-06-01 onward. Ingest time is therefore later than every historical decision time.
Second-leg fields are absent or empty: ok_p is 0 percent populated across every symbol, and there is no spot price, borrow rate, basis, or bid/ask on either leg.
Coverage is 691 of roughly 1215 expected 8-hour intervals over 405 days, with gaps up to 112 hours.
data_constraints.consequence: Causal funding carry cannot be evaluated on this dataset. The current Carry implementation is closed. This cannot be repaired by backfill, because the predicted funding rate is a live-only observable and is not retrievable retrospectively.
data_constraints.review_criterion: Only on a new source carrying publication_ts, or our own forward-recorded series carrying ingest_ts captured at observation time. Indirect reconstruction of the publication moment is explicitly not an acceptable route.

data_constraints.title: The 11 bps research cost floor is fees only and understates realised taker cost by roughly 5 bps
data_constraints.statement: Every hypothesis in this programme was evaluated against an 11 bps single-leg round trip, hardcoded independently in six engines with no derivation. That figure contains two taker fee legs and nothing else. The repository documents a realistic all-in Bybit VIP0 round trip of 0.160 percent, which is 16 bps, and a live operating rule that permits a taker entry only above 0.13 percent per round trip, which is 13 bps. Both exceed the research constant. The gap reconciles to the execution components the constant omits: measured taker slippage of 4.46 bps and spread of 1.1 bps over 29 live round trips.
data_constraints.scope_note: Applies to the cost floor used in research engines, not to live PnL accounting, which is reconciled to the cent against real fills and is unaffected.
evidence: cost_bps_roundtrip: 11 appears in ah019:64, ah041:35, ah046:29, ah048:36, and as cost_bps_both_legs: 22 in simple_pairs:34 and market_neutral_funding_carry:38, with no shared definition and no source.
BOTALIN_RESEARCH_SUMMARY_FOR_EXTERNAL_AI_2026-07-18.md:276 -- conservative taker model 0.250 RT was harsher than the real Bybit VIP0 of about 0.160 RT.
docs/BOTALIN_HANDOFF_2026-07-13_REV6.md:17 -- forensics over 29 valid round trips: taker slip +4.46 bps, spread 1.1 bps, maker slip -1.1 bps, adverse under 2 bps, reconciled to the cent.
Same line records the adopted live rule: taker only when expected edge exceeds 0.13 percent per round trip.
Whether the 1.1 bps spread is already contained inside the 4.46 bps slippage depends on the unrecorded reference price, so the audit adopts the reconciled 16 bps rather than publishing a new sum.

The schedule now exists as a versioned record at data/botalin_fee_schedule_2026-08-05.json and the floor is derived in one shared module, scripts/analysis/cost_model.mjs, which refuses to return a bare number: every value carries its schedule entry, its fee and execution components, and their sources.

The audited 16 bps floor is confirmed as 10.45 fee plus 5.56 execution, and is now known to be a CENTRAL figure rather than a conservative one: the measured all-in median is 16.01, the p75 is 19.19 and the p95 is 25.56.

The existing record therefore stands without re-running. Future tasks must use 16 bps single-leg and 32 bps two-leg, retaining 11/22 only as an optimistic bound for comparison against the historical record. The maker escape route does not open this: the spread is narrower than the maker fee on most liquid symbols, and our own maker-fill probe measured -1.07 bps before fees at t=-9.07. RESOLVED for future work: the floor is derived from a versioned schedule by a shared module as of 2026-08-05. The six engines keep their frozen constants so their published numbers stay reproducible. One thing the resolution added rather than confirmed: the superseded 11 bps sat at the MEDIAN realised fee, not above it, so it was never conservative even as a fee-only figure -- a quarter of positions paid more than 13.6 bps in fees alone.

closure_decisions.subject: FAM.SWEEP_CONTINUATION
closure_decisions.decisive_measurement: Post-sweep continuation rises monotonically with within-symbol notional across nine percentile bands, 4.40 bps below the median to 8.27 bps for the largest one in a thousand, and saturates there. The 5x5 double sort on notional rank and pre-sweep depth response is flat in the depth dimension at every size and horizon; the maximum of 75 reportable cells is 10.27 bps against a 16 bps floor. The extreme cell falls 8.65 bps short at t=8.96 with 2.46 bps detectable, so the shortfall is measured rather than a power problem.
closure_decisions.reopen_criterion: Only on a round-trip cost position below roughly 8 bps, or on a new conditioner that is not derived from the pre-sweep book state and orders the top notional row monotonically. A different percentile cut on the same conditioner is a parameter search and does not qualify.
closure_decisions.notes: The paying tail is real -- 32 percent of AH-048 events at 900s exceeded 11 bps -- but it is dispersion, not a conditional mean, and this closure says only that it is not identifiable in advance. REOPEN ATTEMPTED AND REFUSED 2026-08-05. Hawkes self-excitation intensity from the sweep arrival stream satisfies the FIRST clause of the reopen criterion: it is not derived from the pre-sweep book state, and its within-symbol Spearman against notional rank is -0.04 at every declared decay constant, so it identifies a genuinely different subset. It fails the SECOND clause at all three constants -- the top notional row is flat in intensity and monotone at none of tau 1s, 10s or 60s, with a maximum cell of 6.80 bps against the 16 bps floor. Pooled across notional levels the relation runs mildly the WRONG way, 4.95 down to 4.31 bps, which refutes the cascade thesis rather than leaving it open. A further attempt on the same conditioner at a different decay constant is a parameter search and does not qualify.

closure_decisions.subject: FAM.WEEKLY_CROSS_SECTIONAL_MOMENTUM
closure_decisions.decisive_measurement: Over 187 weeks and 43 symbols the quintile ordering is monotone at 90, 101, 123, 169 and 181 bps, but the long-short spread is 91.1 bps with a standard error of 61.7, t=1.48, against 185 bps detectable at t=3. The published 250 to 410 bps sits 2.6 to 5.2 standard errors above the estimate and is ruled out. The residual has a payoff-trap shape: median 21 bps against a mean of 91, 51 percent of weeks net positive, and a negative net median under the 32 bps stress.
closure_decisions.reopen_criterion: Only on a sample roughly four times this one resolving the spread at t=3 with the quintile ordering intact AND a positive net median under the 32 bps stress. Extending the span alone does not qualify unless survivorship is addressed, since the present universe is selected on surviving three and a half years.
closure_decisions.notes: CLOSED_UNDERPOWERED, not CLOSED_MEASURED. The published effect is ruled out; the residual is not, and this record must never be cited as showing that cross-sectional momentum does not exist.

closure_decisions.subject: METHOD.MAKER_EXECUTION_AS_COST_ESCAPE
closure_decisions.decisive_measurement: Two independent closures. From the fee schedule: the spread is narrower than the maker fee on most liquid symbols, with a measured median spread of 1.12 bps, so a passive order captures less than it pays before any market risk. From our own measurement: the maker-fill probe recorded -1.07 bps across 4,965 placements at a 28.7 percent fill rate BEFORE fees, at t=-9.07, with the forward move against the filled side roughly threefold the 0.72 bps half-spread captured.
closure_decisions.reopen_criterion: Only on a materially different fee position -- a maker rebate or a venue whose maker fee sits below the prevailing spread on our universe. A better queue model does not qualify, because adverse selection and not queue position is what the probe measured.

closure_decisions.subject: METHOD.DIRECTION_FROM_PRICE_HISTORY
closure_decisions.decisive_measurement: Thirty-five hypotheses inferring direction from past price have been rejected, none passing. The literature supplies the mechanism rather than merely agreeing: Bajgrowicz and Scaillet found over 7,846 rules and a century of DJIA data that even in-sample profits are completely offset by low transaction costs and that the future best rule could never have been selected ex ante; Marshall, Young and Rose found candlestick value vanishes against a generated-OHLC bootstrap, and the surviving positive results flip with the exit convention rather than the entry pattern.
closure_decisions.reopen_criterion: Only on a mechanism that names who pays and why, tested at a horizon where the round trip is under 5 percent of the available move. A new pattern formulation on the same data is a documented structural variant at best and does not qualify.
closure_decisions.source_of_record: literature review 2026-08-04 against the programme record

closure_decisions.subject: METHOD.PRIORITISE_BY_IN_SAMPLE_RANK
closure_decisions.decisive_measurement: Across three independent 40-week transitions over 54 enumerated rules, the period-1 winner landed at the 25th percentile of period 2, beat the median in zero of three, and went outright negative every time after averaging +190 bps in the window that selected it. Mean Spearman on the independent series is 0.078 against 0.193 detectable. All three winners were decile portfolios, the most concentrated width -- an overfitting signature rather than a market fact.
closure_decisions.reopen_criterion: Only on a persistence test with at least ten independent transitions showing a resolvably positive mean Spearman AND the period-1 winner beating the period-2 median in a majority. Rolling windows do not qualify: at 90 percent overlap their transition count is not a sample size.
closure_decisions.notes: Three transitions give a naive sign-test probability of 1/8, so this does not establish the finding alone; its weight is corroborative with Bajgrowicz and Scaillet. It closes a METHOD, not a family: it does not invalidate the thirty-seven closures, because failure is far easier to establish than success. It bears on the opposite direction -- a candidate topping an in-sample leaderboard has thereby earned close to nothing.

closure_decisions.subject: FAM.CARRY
closure_decisions.decisive_measurement: Funding premium and hedgeability do not coexist. Conditional funding on the unhedgeable subset gave +7.06 bps net, but concentration analysis showed a single asset at 151 percent of the total and remove-best took it to -4.48. On the hedgeable subset the 168-hour gross of 14.9 bps falls short of the 22 bps two-leg floor, which the cost audit has since raised to 32.
closure_decisions.reopen_criterion: Only on a venue where a persistent funding premium and a tradeable spot leg exist on the SAME asset, evidenced before any return is measured. A larger asset universe on the present venues does not qualify.

closure_decisions.subject: FAM.CROSS_EXCHANGE_LEADLAG
closure_decisions.decisive_measurement: The archive contains exactly ONE tick-resolution venue. Of 27 catalogued sources, EDGE.DATA.TICKS is the only one at tick granularity; EDGE.DATA.HL_CASCADE, the only other venue present, records at 60s. There is no Binance source at all. A lead-lag measured in hundreds of milliseconds requires two millisecond-stamped streams and we hold one, so the question cannot be posed at any cost threshold.
closure_decisions.reopen_criterion: All three, together. (a) A second venue recorded at tick or L2-event resolution with its own ingest timestamp captured at observation time, not the venue-reported timestamp. (b) A MEASURED clock offset between the two streams, published with its dispersion: two venues timestamps are not comparable until the offset is known, and an unmeasured offset would make any apparent lag indistinguishable from clock skew. (c) A pre-declared expectation that the cross-venue spread exceeds the audited 16 bps round trip for long enough to act, since our own measured 10-second dispersion is 3.6 bps and a spread below the floor is untradeable however reliably it is detected.
closure_decisions.source_of_record: direction triage 2026-08-05, verified against the catalogued source inventory
closure_decisions.notes: DATA_BLOCKED, not CLOSED_MEASURED: the hypothesis is well posed and the data is absent. Clause (b) is the one most likely to be skipped and is the reason this is recorded at all — a lead-lag study that omits clock alignment measures its own infrastructure, which is the same failure mode as DC.FUNDING.SETTLEMENT_TS_ONLY in a different guise.

closure_decisions.subject: FAM.CROSS_SECTIONAL_SECTOR_IMBALANCE
closure_decisions.decisive_measurement: No sector taxonomy exists anywhere in the archive. A scan of all 27 catalogued data sources found zero carrying a sector, category, taxonomy or classification field. Sector-relative return cannot be computed without one, so the construct has no input.
closure_decisions.reopen_criterion: A versioned, POINT-IN-TIME sector taxonomy: each assignment carries the date from which it held, and reassignments create a new record rather than overwriting the old one. Applying present-day labels backwards is look-ahead — a coin relabelled from one sector to another in 2026 would carry that label through 2024 data and encode knowledge of what it became. The taxonomy must also state its assignment rule, so that membership is auditable rather than editorial. A vendor list without dated history does not qualify.
closure_decisions.source_of_record: direction triage 2026-08-05, verified against the catalogued source inventory
closure_decisions.notes: Distinct from CD.WEEKLY_XSECT_MOMENTUM, which closed a cross-sectional signal on measured grounds; this one has never been measured because it has no input. If a taxonomy arrives, the underpowered finding recorded against the weekly cross-section applies to the sector variant too and should be checked before spending the data.

closure_decisions.subject: METHOD.ORDER_FLOW_IMBALANCE_AS_DIRECTION
closure_decisions.decisive_measurement: Parent order flow imbalance carries +0.073 bps out of sample at a gross t of 0.50 over 56,073 observations, against an audited 16 bps round trip. Reconstructed at the frozen 100 ms burst gap over 553,632 parent orders. The same signal used SUPPRESSIVELY rather than directionally is the only surviving result in the programme: the execution guard measures +0.715 bps of avoided adverse move at t=20.1 over 779,540 observations with all three checks PASS.
closure_decisions.reopen_criterion: Only on order-book data at EVENT resolution rather than snapshots. The canonical construct measures limit adds, cancels and market orders at the touch between consecutive events; our book is written at a measured 10,000 ms median cadence, which is not that object. A reopen must also carry the staleness curve required by the G3 guard protocol, since a feed change that does not move the mean decision staleness changes nothing. Recomputing the same snapshot-based quantity at a different aggregation is a parameter search and does not qualify.
closure_decisions.source_of_record: TASK-AH-046 out-of-sample result, reclassified by the direction triage 2026-08-05
closure_decisions.notes: This closes a METHOD in one use and confirms it in another, which is why it is recorded rather than left implicit. It matches Cont, Kukanov and Stoikov exactly: order flow imbalance explains the repricing happening NOW, with a slope inversely proportional to depth. From that it follows that stepping into the move is costly -- which is the guard -- and it does not follow that the next move is predictable, which is AH-046. The programme measured both halves independently before reading the paper. OFI is hereby fixed as a filtering instrument in the guard lane and may not be proposed again as a direction source without satisfying the reopen criterion.

closure_decisions.subject: GAP.NEWS.TAGGER_V2
closure_decisions.decisive_measurement: The causal timestamp check PASSED and the lane is blocked anyway. first_seen_at is present and populated on 100 percent of 227 forward-lab events, written as a mandatory field by news_recorder.mjs, which is live. Three further findings each close the lane independently. (1) Detection delay, recorded per event as detect_delay_ms, has a median of 12.2 minutes: only 10.7 percent of events are seen within a minute and 21.9 percent within five, with p75 at 401 minutes and p95 at 1,169. The p05 is NEGATIVE at -464 minutes, confirming on live data the future-dated published_at already recorded against this source. (2) Joinability to our market data is 1 event of 94: of 104 symbols extracted from mechanism events only AERGOUSDT exists in the 40-symbol tick archive, because 75 of the 94 are new listings and a newly listed symbol has no prior history by construction. (3) The symbol extractor is broken -- the most frequent extracted token is "UTC" at five occurrences, alongside "00AM", "APPSTOCK", "CBK", "FLIP", "OL", parsed out of title text such as "at 10:00AM UTC".
closure_decisions.reopen_criterion: All three, together, and the third is the one that decides. (1) SYMBOL EXTRACTION: zero junk tokens in the symbols field, verified against a symbol registry with a measured false-positive rate; "UTC" and "00AM" must not appear. (2) UNIVERSE COVERAGE: more than 30 percent of mechanism events joinable to the local tick archive. Note this is near self-defeating for listings, which have no prior history by construction, so the reachable subset is delistings and margin changes on symbols already recorded. (3) ECONOMIC THRESHOLD: direct evidence that the residual price move remaining AFTER our actual measured detection delay, taken at the p50 of the ingest lag rather than an assumed one, still exceeds the audited 16 bps round trip. A faster feed does not qualify on its own; the reopen must show the money that survives the delay we actually have.
closure_decisions.source_of_record: read-only audit of /mnt/data-vol/news-lab/events.jsonl and the historical archive, 2026-08-05
closure_decisions.notes: The check we set in advance was the wrong check, and saying so is the point of recording this. first_seen_at was treated as the blocker and it is present; the lane dies on delay, joinability and extraction quality instead. The three are not independent: removing the delay leaves nothing to join, fixing the extractor moves joinable events from one to about two, and widening the recorded universe still cannot give a new listing a price history. The historical archive is separately unusable and honestly self-labelled -- 1,251 rows carrying first_seen_at=null with not_forward=true and not_tradeable_timing=true on every one.

closure_decisions.subject: FAM.FUNDING_VELOCITY_AND_CLEARING_WINDOWS
closure_decisions.decisive_measurement: Three declared numbers on 35,029 60-second snapshots over 232 assets, universe the top 30 by median notional volume. (1) Movement in the 30 minutes either side of the 8-hour funding settlement is 60.75 bps against 64.14 in matched control windows -- a difference of -3.38 bps at t=-1.23, so settlement windows move if anything LESS, against a rebalancing thesis that predicts more. An independent recomputation on BTC alone in a different language gave +0.84 bps, equally indistinguishable from zero. (2) Funding velocity IS orthogonal to funding level, within-asset Spearman +0.073 with no asset above 0.5, so the conditioner is genuinely independent information. (3) Forward 60-minute move by velocity quintile reaches at most 6.07 bps in absolute terms against a 16 bps floor, is not monotone, and carries a q4-q0 spread of -4.47 bps.
closure_decisions.reopen_criterion: Only at a materially longer measurement horizon than 30 minutes, and only with a velocity construct that does not degenerate. At 30 minutes this funding series has roughly two states rather than five: it is quantised and mean-reverting, so 60 percent of observations tie even when velocity is computed as a slope over the window rather than an endpoint difference. A reopen must first demonstrate that its chosen horizon yields balanced buckets, reporting the tie fraction, before any return is measured. Re-running the same 30-minute construct on a longer archive does not qualify: the observation count is already large enough to have answered.
closure_decisions.notes: CLOSED_MEASURED and not CLOSED_UNDERPOWERED, which contradicts the prediction made the previous day. The archive spans only 25 days and carries 73 settlements, so underpowered was the expected verdict; but 34,950 velocity observations give standard errors near 2 bps, placing a 16 bps effect roughly eight standard errors from what was measured. Short span did not mean small sample. Waiting for the recorder to reach its designed 30 days would add 20 percent to a sample that has already answered. This closes funding VELOCITY and the settlement window; it does not touch open interest, the oracle-mark gap, or the exchange-reported premium field, which is a distinct quantity from mark minus oracle. The open-interest hypothesis is the one the recorder was built for -- its header states the design thesis as cascade equals OI collapse plus oracle/mark divergence.

closure_decisions.subject: FAM.OI_COLLAPSE_ON_RISE
closure_decisions.decisive_measurement: The degeneracy check passed cleanly -- worst quintile imbalance 1.06 against 16.08 for funding velocity, with dOI 96.4 percent distinct over 1,050,870 observations -- so the event study ran on a non-degenerate sort. It refuted the declared direction. Over 283 non-overlapping events on 29 assets, shorting a rising price whose open interest collapsed returned -5.80 bps at 5 minutes with t=-1.93: the price CONTINUED upward rather than reverting, the same shape as TASK-AH-048. Standard error is 3.00 bps, so a +16 bps reversion sits 7.3 standard errors from the measurement and is excluded. Severity quintiles are not monotone and the largest OI collapses give the least reversion (+4.55). Conditioning on a top-quintile mark-oracle gap made it worse, -8.69 bps at t=-2.32.
closure_decisions.reopen_criterion: Only on the mirror event -- price DOWN with open interest collapsing, traded long -- and only at roughly five to six times the present sample, on the order of 140 days rather than 25, which is what it takes to bring the standard error from 4.84 to about 2.06 and separate +9.82 from the 16 bps floor at t=3. A reopen must ALSO show a monotone severity profile, which the present sample does not have. Re-running the declared primary is a silent retry: its direction is excluded at 7.3 standard errors. Waiting for the recorder to reach its designed 30 days adds 20 percent and does not qualify.
closure_decisions.notes: This was the last directional target on the open-directions register, and it was the only surviving hypothesis whose data had been collected on purpose for it. Under the criterion set before the run -- reversion below 16 bps or noise closes the loop -- the directional-alpha research programme is complete. The mirror at 15 minutes is the single unresolved figure at 1.28 standard errors from the floor, and it must not be chased: it is a non-primary horizon of a non-primary event set selected after the fact, which is exactly the selection CD.SELECTION_ON_INSAMPLE_RANK measured to be worthless. Recorded separately as a useful by-product: the mark-oracle gap carries a standard deviation of 13.06 bps, an order of magnitude wider than the perp-spot basis at 1.4 to 1.7 bps on majors, so the two are different objects and LAW.BASIS.LIQUID_PERP_BELOW_COST does not speak to this one.

closure_decisions.subject: FAM.MOMENTUM_VOL_EXPANSION_BREAKOUT
closure_decisions.decisive_measurement: The balance gate passed first -- vol_burst 100 percent distinct with a bucket ratio of 1.0005 and a range from 1.63 to 12.11 -- so the sort is real and the measurement stands. Over 9,714 non-overlapping events on 16 symbols and 99 days, entering WITH a volume-burst break of the 24-bar extreme returns -3.29 bps at 45 minutes with t=-3.58, and -3.50 bps at 30 minutes with t=-4.59. The detectable size at t=3 is 2.76 bps, so this is a resolved negative in the direction opposite to the one declared: the break reverts rather than continues. Under the frozen exits, a 1 percent stop and a 45-minute time stop, the realised mean is -2.80 bps with 15.8 percent stopped out. The burst-size profile is not monotone, and the largest bursts at 12.08x flip to +3.96 bps at t=1.51, unresolved and still a quarter of the floor.
closure_decisions.reopen_criterion: Not on this construction at any threshold: the effect is resolved negative at t=-3.58 and a different burst or expansion cut is a parameter search. A reopen would require a DIFFERENT event definition that preserves the single-participant property -- the tick-level parent reconstruction of AH-046 rather than a five-minute bar -- together with a pre-declared expectation stating why aggregation would not destroy it this time. The mirror, fading the break at +3.29 bps, does not qualify: it is a fifth of the floor and it was discovered on train after the opposite direction was declared.
closure_decisions.notes: The pre-recorded expectation was FALSIFIED, and downward. The task recorded +8.27 bps before the engine existed, taken from LAW.FLOW.SWEEP_CONTINUATION_SATURATES; the measurement is -3.29, which is 12.6 standard errors below the prior. The saturation law does not carry from tick-level parent sweeps to bar-level volume bursts and the sign inverts. The mechanism is that a parent sweep is ONE participant crossing levels inside 100 ms and its continuation is that participant own impact still resolving, whereas a five-minute bar is an aggregate of many participants including everyone fading the move. The two events resemble each other only in description. This is the first pre-registered expectation in the programme to be falsified, which is the reason recording it in advance was worth the effort.
